observations: Photo 0 shows a Nikon Z fc mirrorless camera body with silver top plate, black grip, and lens cap marked 'Nikon Z mount'.
Photo 1 shows the top shutter speed dial, 'Nikon' branding on the prism, and 'Z fc' on the top right; an attached lens with a manual aperture ring is visible.
Photo 2 shows the full kit: camera body with lens, Nikon EN-EL25a battery, Nikon MH-32 charger, body cap, rear lens cap, and a front lens cap marked 'TTArtisan APS-C 35mm F2.0'.

claims.claim: Nikon z fc is a retro-inspired, slr-style mirrorless camera featuring a 20.9-megapixel aps-c
claims.evidence: photo 0 and photo 1 show the Nikon Z fc body matching that description
photo 0 and photo 1 clearly show Nikon branding, not Canon

risks.risk: Camera does not power on or fire the shutter
risks.proof: Video of the camera turning on, navigating the menu, and taking a photo

risks.risk: Lens has fungus, haze, or scratches on the elements
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the front and rear lens elements under bright light

risks.risk: Battery does not hold a charge
risks.proof: Video of the battery charging and powering the camera

risks.risk: Shutter count is high or the mechanism is worn
risks.proof: Screenshot of shutter count from the camera menu or sample photo EXIF data

proof_requests: Video of the camera powering on, taking a photo, and reviewing the image
Close-up photos of the lens front and rear elements with a flashlight
Video of the battery charging and the camera running on battery
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as a Nikon Z fc from the photos; the seller's Canon claim is contradicted by visible branding, but the camera can still be priced at its worst case pending proof of function.
